clips.send: A mother sends this to her teenage son who keeps saying he can't, hoping one Henry Ford line rewires his belief before anyone else's doubt does - hope mixed with urgency.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the voice that told you "you can't" probably wasn't yours - a parent or teacher said it once when you were a kid, and you never questioned it again.

Henry Ford, one of the richest men who ever lived, put the fix in six words: if you believe you can, or you believe you can't, either way, you're right.

It isn't motivation. It's a program running in the background, deciding outcomes before you even try - and nobody hands you a new one until you notice the old one running.

What did you decide about yourself before you were old enough to question it?
